questions.question: Which of the following gases is consistently seen to be most abundant in a volcanic eruption?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Water vapour**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water Vapour**__- It is consistently seen to be the most abundant in a volcanic eruption. 
 
• It occurs when lava and gas are discharged from the vent of the volcano.
 
• The eruption majorly emits water vapor into the atmosphere. But other gases like-Carbon dioxide, Sulphur Dioxide, Hydrogen Sulfide are also emitted.
 
• 'Glowing avalanche' is the most dangerous type of volcanic eruption.
 
• The magma which is freshly erupted forms a hot pyroclastic flow. This flow generally has a temperature of up to 1,200 degrees.
 
• The flow sometimes takes a speed of up to several hundred kilometers per hour. It can reach as far as 40 km from the original disaster site.

questions.question: Which leader gave us the C R Formula?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **C. Rajagopalachari**__ gave us the C R Formula. 
 
• This Formula is also known as Rajaji Formula.
 
• During the Second World War, the British government states that if the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League resolved their differences, Indian statehood would be possible.
 
• The Muslim League, however, was demanding a separate nation of Pakistan for the Muslims. Indian National Congress was against the partition of the country.
 
• C Rajagopalachari who was a member of INC proposed a set of plans called the C R Formula or Rajaji Formula to break this deadlock between the two major political parties in India.
 
• To summarise the formula, the Congress was requested to hold the plebiscite in the regions where Muslims made a majority.
 
• Muslim league was supposed to support the congress’s demand for complete freedom from Britishers and then the majority provinces would go to a plebiscite.

questions.question: Name the only metal that is antibacterial.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Copper**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper**__ is the only metal that is antibacterial. 
 
• It is also called "germ-killer" because its alloys show antibacterial, antiviral and anti-fungal properties.
 
• It is scientifically proven that copper continuously kills more than 99.9% of the microbes that have caused infections within two hours of contact. This is called ‘contact killing’.
 
• Copper is also proved to completely destroy the bacteria’s DNA which prevents bacteria from developing a resistance to copper.
 
• Copper is the only solid metal touch surface to have been approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency in recognition of these antimicrobial properties.
 
• The atomic number of Copper-29. Symbol- Cu

questions.question: Which component performs the task of capturing oxygen in the blood?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Haemoglobin**__ performs the task of capturing oxygen in the blood. 
 
• They are basically the proteins inside RBCs and carry oxygen to cells. They also carry carbon dioxide to the lungs.
 
• It is made up of four symmetrical subunits and four heme groups.
 
• Irons which are associated with the heme actually bind oxygen.
 
• Please note that it is the same iron in haemoglobin that gives blood its red color.
 
• Red blood cells-The are made in the bone marrow and it helps in carrying oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.
 
• Chlorophyll- It is a green photosynthetic pigment that is found in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.
 
• **White blood cells**- These are also called leukocytes. They are involved in providing immunity to the body or protecting the body against both infectious disease and foreign particles.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is NOT transmitted from one person to another?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Cirrhosis**__ is NOT transmitted from one person to another. 
 
• It is a condition in which the liver of our body can not function properly, possibly because of long-term damage.
 
• The normal tissue is replaced by scar tissue in such conditions.
 
• However, it can have various reasons but alcohol consumption remains the second most common cause of liver cirrhosis after the hepatitis C virus.
 
• **Hepatitis B**-It is also a liver infection which is caused by the hepatitis B virus that's easily preventable by a vaccine, unlike Cirrhosis. It is spread by exposure to infected bodily fluids.
 
• **Syphilis**-It is a bacterial infection usually spread by sexual contact.
 
• **AIDS**-It interferes with the body's ability to fight against infections or in other words affect immunity. The virus can be transmitted through contact with infected blood, semen or vaginal fluids.

questions.question: When did the Vikrama Era begin?
questions.solution:
The **Vikrama Era** began in __**57 BC**__.

 
• It is said (as per the Jain book Kālakācāryakathā) that Vikram Era was founded King Vikramāditya gained victory over the Śakas.
 
• However, V. A. Smith and D. R. Bhandarkar (Archaeologist) believed that Chandragupta II adopted the title of Vikramaditya. It was he who changed the era's name to "Vikrama Samvat".
 
• Vikram Samvat is also considered to be the official calendar of Nepal.
 
• The first day of the Vikram Samvat calendar is celebrated after Diwali in the states of Gujarat and Maharashtra.
